name: World War I
summary: The Allied Powers, chiefly France, Britain, Russia, Italy and from 1917 the United States, fought the Central Powers of Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand set off a chain of alliances. Trench deadlock in the west, vast movement in the east and new fronts at Gallipoli, in Arabia and in Mesopotamia ended with the Central Powers' collapse in 1918, after about 9 million soldiers had died. The war destroyed four empires, brought revolution to Russia and redrew the map of Europe and the Middle East.

steps.label: Aug to Sep 1914
steps.title: The Schlieffen Plan and the Marne
steps.text: Germany invaded neutral Belgium to outflank the French armies, bringing Britain into the war. Kluck's First Army swept through Belgium toward Paris, but Joffre's French and British counterattack on the Marne forced the Germans back to the Aisne. A race to the sea followed, and by December a line of trenches ran from the Channel to Switzerland.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moves.label: British Expeditionary Force retreats from Mons

events.name: Siege of Liege
events.text: German siege guns reduced the Belgian forts, but the defence cost the German plan precious days.

events.name: First Battle of the Marne
events.text: The Allied counterattack stopped the German advance short of Paris and ended hopes of a quick war.

events.name: First Battle of Ypres
events.text: British, French and Belgian troops held Ypres, fixing the northern end of the trench line.

steps.label: Aug to Dec 1914
steps.title: Tannenberg and Galicia
steps.text: Russia invaded East Prussia sooner than Germany expected, but Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircled Samsonov's Second Army at Tannenberg and drove Rennenkampf out at the Masurian Lakes. Further south Russian armies routed the Austro-Hungarians in Galicia, took Lemberg and besieged Przemysl. In November the Ottoman Empire entered the war on the side of the Central Powers.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.name: Battle of Tannenberg
events.text: Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircled the Russian Second Army and took about 90,000 prisoners.

events.name: Battle of Galicia
events.text: Russia defeated Austria-Hungary, took Lemberg and besieged Przemysl.

steps.label: Feb 1915 to Jan 1916
steps.title: Gallipoli
steps.text: Britain and France tried to force the Dardanelles and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. After the fleet was stopped at the Narrows, Hamilton landed British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops at Helles and Anzac Cove, but Ottoman forces under Liman von Sanders and Mustafa Kemal pinned them on the beaches until the Allies withdrew. In the Caucasus Enver's winter offensive was destroyed at Sarikamish, and in 1915 the Ottoman government began the deportations and mass killings of Armenians.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moves.label: Landings at Helles and Anzac Cove

events.name: Naval attack on the Dardanelles
events.text: Mines sank three Allied battleships on 18 March and the fleet turned back.

events.name: Gallipoli campaign
events.text: After eight months and about half a million casualties on both sides, the Allies evacuated the peninsula.

events.name: Battle of Sarikamish
events.text: Enver's winter offensive against Russia ended in disaster, with most of the Ottoman Third Army lost.

steps.label: May to Dec 1915
steps.title: The Great Retreat and the fall of Serbia
steps.text: A German and Austro-Hungarian breakthrough under Mackensen at Gorlice-Tarnow broke the Russian front, and by autumn the Russians had lost Poland, Lithuania and Galicia. Italy joined the Allies in May but stalled on the Isonzo. In October Bulgaria joined the Central Powers and Serbia was overrun, its army retreating across the Albanian mountains to Corfu.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.name: Gorlice-Tarnow Offensive
events.text: The Central Powers broke the Russian front and began a retreat of hundreds of kilometres.

events.name: Fall of Warsaw
events.text: German troops entered Warsaw on 5 August as Russia abandoned Poland.

events.name: Conquest of Serbia
events.text: German, Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian armies overran Serbia in two months.

steps.label: Feb to Nov 1916
steps.title: Verdun, Jutland and the Somme
steps.text: Falkenhayn attacked Verdun to bleed the French army white, and Petain held the city through ten months of fighting. Haig's British offensive on the Somme lost about 57,000 casualties on its first day and gained only a few kilometres. At sea the British Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet met once, at Jutland, after which the German fleet stayed in port.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.name: Battle of Verdun
events.text: France held Verdun at a cost of over 700,000 casualties on both sides.

events.name: Battle of Jutland
events.text: Britain lost more ships, but the German fleet never again challenged British control of the North Sea.

events.name: Battle of the Somme
events.text: Over a million men were killed or wounded for a few kilometres of ground.

steps.label: Jun 1916 to Jan 1917
steps.title: Brusilov's offensive and Romania
steps.text: Brusilov's surprise attack along a wide front shattered the Austro-Hungarian armies in Volhynia and Bukovina, the greatest Allied success of the year. Encouraged, Romania joined the Allies in August and invaded Transylvania, but Falkenhayn and Mackensen counterattacked from two sides and took Bucharest in December. The Romanian army held on only in Moldavia with Russian help.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moves.label: Southwestern Front breaks through at Lutsk
Ninth Army through the Carpathian passes

events.name: Brusilov Offensive
events.text: Russia inflicted about a million casualties on Austria-Hungary, which never fully recovered.

events.name: Fall of Bucharest
events.text: The Central Powers took the Romanian capital on 6 December and seized its oil and grain.

steps.label: Apr 1916 to Dec 1917
steps.title: Kut, the Arab Revolt and Baghdad
steps.text: In Mesopotamia Townshend's British and Indian force, beaten at Ctesiphon, surrendered at Kut in April 1916. In June Sharif Hussein of Mecca launched the Arab Revolt, and his son Faisal, with the British officer T. E. Lawrence, moved north along the Red Sea and took Aqaba in July 1917. Maude retook Kut and captured Baghdad in March 1917, and Allenby broke the Gaza line at Beersheba and entered Jerusalem in December.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moves.label: Advance up the Tigris to Baghdad

events.name: Siege of Kut
events.text: About 13,000 British and Indian troops surrendered to the Ottomans after a five-month siege.

events.name: Capture of Aqaba
events.text: Arab forces took the port from the landward side, opening a supply line for the revolt.

events.name: Fall of Baghdad
events.text: Maude's army entered Baghdad on 11 March 1917.

steps.label: Mar to Dec 1917
steps.title: Revolution, America and Caporetto
steps.text: Revolution overthrew the Tsar in March, and after a failed summer offensive the Bolsheviks seized power in November and sought peace. The United States declared war in April and Pershing began shipping an army to France, while Haig's offensive at Passchendaele ground through mud for little gain. In October a German and Austro-Hungarian attack at Caporetto broke the Italian front and drove it back to the Piave.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.name: Battle of Passchendaele
events.text: Months of attacks in deep mud cost about half a million casualties for a few kilometres.

events.name: Battle of Caporetto
events.text: Italy lost about 300,000 men, most as prisoners, before holding on the Piave.

events.name: October Revolution
events.text: Lenin's Bolsheviks took power in Petrograd and moved to take Russia out of the war.

steps.label: Mar to Jul 1918
steps.title: Brest-Litovsk and the Spring Offensive
steps.text: Soviet Russia signed away Poland, the Baltic lands and Ukraine at Brest-Litovsk, and Romania made peace soon after. Ludendorff used the divisions freed in the east for a series of offensives in France that drove deep salients toward Amiens and the Marne. Under Foch as Allied supreme commander, French, British and growing American forces held, and in July the Second Battle of the Marne turned the tide.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

fronts.label: German occupation limit in the east, 1918

events.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
events.text: Soviet Russia left the war, giving up a third of its European population.

events.name: Operation Michael
events.text: The largest German offensive of the war gained ground but failed to split the Allies.

events.name: Second Battle of the Marne
events.text: The last German offensive failed and Foch's counterattack began the Allied advance.

steps.label: Aug to Nov 1918
steps.title: The Hundred Days and the armistice
steps.text: From Amiens on 8 August the Allies attacked all along the Western Front and broke the Hindenburg Line, while Pershing's Americans pushed through the Argonne. In the east Allenby destroyed the Ottoman armies at Megiddo and Faisal's Arab forces entered Damascus, Franchet d'Esperey broke out from Salonika and forced Bulgaria to quit, and British troops advanced up the Tigris toward Mosul. The Ottoman Empire and Austria-Hungary signed armistices, and Germany followed on 11 November 1918.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

moves.label: Megiddo and the drive to Damascus

events.name: Battle of Amiens
events.text: Ludendorff called 8 August the black day of the German army.

events.name: Battle of Megiddo
events.text: Allenby's breakthrough destroyed the Ottoman armies in Palestine.

events.name: Armistice of Compiegne
events.text: Germany signed the armistice in a railway carriage and the guns fell silent at 11 am on 11 November.

name: Russian Civil War
summary: After the Bolsheviks seized power in 1917, their Red Army fought a loose alliance of White armies, backed at times by Allied intervention forces, across the former Russian Empire. The Reds held the central heartland and its railways while the Whites attacked from Siberia, the south, the Baltic and the north, and one by one were defeated by 1920. About 7 to 12 million people died, mostly civilians from famine, disease and terror, and the victory produced the Soviet Union in 1922.

steps.label: Nov 1917 to Apr 1918
steps.title: Revolution and the first Whites
steps.text: Lenin's Bolsheviks seized Petrograd in November 1917, dissolved the elected Constituent Assembly and made peace with Germany at Brest-Litovsk. Red Guards took Kiev and much of the south, and the government moved to Moscow. On the Don, Kornilov and Alekseyev raised the anti-Bolshevik Volunteer Army, which marched across the frozen steppe to Yekaterinodar, where Kornilov was killed.

moves.label: The Ice March of the Volunteer Army

events.name: October Revolution
events.text: The Bolsheviks stormed the Winter Palace and took power in Petrograd.

events.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
events.text: Soviet Russia left the World War at the cost of Ukraine, Poland and the Baltic lands.

events.name: Assault on Yekaterinodar
events.text: The Volunteer Army's attack failed and Kornilov was killed by a shell.

steps.label: May to Dec 1918
steps.title: The fronts take shape
steps.text: In May the Czechoslovak Legion, strung out along the Trans-Siberian Railway, revolted and handed the Volga and Siberia to anti-Bolshevik governments. Trotsky built a conscript Red Army and retook Kazan in September, while Allied troops landed at Murmansk and Arkhangelsk. In November Admiral Kolchak took power in Omsk as Supreme Ruler, and in the south Denikin's Volunteer Army cleared the Kuban. In July the Bolsheviks killed the former Tsar and his family at Yekaterinburg.

events.name: Revolt of the Czechoslovak Legion
events.text: About 40,000 former prisoners of war seized the railway from the Volga to Vladivostok.

events.name: Battle of Kazan
events.text: The first major Red victory, won by Trotsky's reorganised army.

events.name: Killing of the imperial family
events.text: Nicholas II, his wife and five children were shot by Bolshevik guards on 17 July.

steps.label: Mar to Oct 1919
steps.title: The White high tide
steps.text: Kolchak's spring offensive reached within reach of the Volga before Frunze's counterattack drove it back across the Urals. In the summer Denikin launched his march on Moscow, taking Kharkiv, Kiev, Kursk and in October Orel, while Wrangel captured Tsaritsyn. In the northwest Yudenich advanced to the outskirts of Petrograd. All three White thrusts peaked in October and were thrown back.

events.name: Capture of Tsaritsyn
events.text: Wrangel took the Volga city in June, linking the White south toward Kolchak's front.

events.name: Battle of Orel
events.text: The Red counterattack at Orel and Kromy broke Denikin's drive about 380 km from Moscow.

events.name: Defence of Petrograd
events.text: Trotsky rallied the city's defenders and Yudenich's army fell back into Estonia.

steps.label: Nov 1919 to Nov 1920
steps.title: The collapse of the Whites
steps.text: Kolchak's armies disintegrated along the Trans-Siberian, and he was handed over and shot at Irkutsk in February 1920. Denikin's forces fled to Novorossiysk and evacuated to Crimea, where Wrangel took command. A Red drive on Warsaw in the Polish-Soviet War was defeated by Pilsudski in August, but in November Frunze stormed the Perekop isthmus and Wrangel's army left Crimea by sea for Constantinople.

events.name: Execution of Kolchak
events.text: Handed over by the Czechoslovaks, the White Supreme Ruler was shot at Irkutsk on 7 February.

events.name: Battle of Warsaw
events.text: Polish forces under Pilsudski routed the Red Army and ended the hope of carrying revolution west.

events.name: Battle of Perekop
events.text: The Red Army broke the fortified isthmus and about 150,000 people left Crimea with Wrangel.

steps.label: Feb 1921 to Dec 1922
steps.title: Last battles and the Soviet Union
steps.text: The Red Army invaded Georgia in February 1921, and in March it crushed the Kronstadt sailors' revolt across the ice while peasant risings were suppressed and famine killed millions. In the Far East, Blyukher's army beat the last Whites at Volochayevka and Japanese troops withdrew, and the Reds entered Vladivostok in October 1922. In December 1922 the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was proclaimed.

moves.label: Assault across the ice on Kronstadt

events.name: Kronstadt rebellion
events.text: Sailors who had backed the revolution demanded free soviets and were crushed in March 1921.

events.name: Battle of Volochayevka
events.text: The decisive Red victory in the Far East opened the road to Vladivostok.

events.name: Formation of the USSR
events.text: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia joined as the Soviet Union on 30 December 1922.

name: Turkish War of Independence
summary: After the Ottoman defeat in 1918 the Allies occupied Constantinople and Greece landed at Smyrna, and Mustafa Kemal organised a national movement in Anatolia that rejected the Treaty of Sevres. Nationalist armies defeated Armenia in the east, pushed France out of Cilicia and, after hard battles at Inonu and Sakarya, routed the Greek army in 1922. The Treaty of Lausanne recognised the new Turkish state, and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed in 1923.

steps.label: May 1919 to Dec 1920
steps.title: Occupation and the national movement
steps.text: Greek troops landed at Smyrna in May 1919, and days later Mustafa Kemal arrived at Samsun and rallied resistance at congresses in Erzurum and Sivas. When the Allies occupied Constantinople in March 1920, a Grand National Assembly opened in Ankara, and it rejected the Treaty of Sevres that partitioned Anatolia. Greek forces pushed inland to Bursa and Usak, while Karabekir defeated Armenia in the east and nationalists fought the French in Cilicia.

moves.label: Greek army from Smyrna to Bursa

events.name: Greek landing at Smyrna
events.text: The Greek occupation of Smyrna in May 1919 sparked Turkish armed resistance.

events.name: Grand National Assembly opens
events.text: The Ankara assembly declared itself the government of the nation on 23 April 1920.

events.name: Treaty of Sevres
events.text: The Sultan's government accepted a partition of Anatolia that the nationalists refused to recognise.

steps.label: Jan to Sep 1921
steps.title: Inonu and Sakarya
steps.text: Ismet Pasha checked two Greek advances at Inonu in January and March 1921. In July a larger Greek offensive won at Kutahya and Eskisehir and marched on Ankara, but Kemal, now commander in chief, held a line on the Sakarya river for three weeks until the exhausted Greeks withdrew. Soon after, France and Soviet Russia made peace with Ankara, freeing the nationalists to turn west.

moves.label: Turkish army stands on the Sakarya
Greek withdrawal to Eskisehir and Afyon

events.name: Second Battle of Inonu
events.text: Ismet's victory in April 1921 gave the new army confidence and its commander his later surname.

events.name: Battle of Kutahya-Eskisehir
events.text: The Greek army took both towns in July and the Turks fell back east of the Sakarya.

events.name: Battle of Sakarya
events.text: After 21 days of fighting the Greek advance on Ankara was halted for good.

steps.label: Aug to Oct 1922
steps.title: The Great Offensive and Smyrna
steps.text: On 26 August 1922 Kemal launched the Great Offensive against the Greek line near Afyon and broke it within days at Dumlupinar. The Greek army fled to the coast and was evacuated, and Turkish cavalry entered Smyrna on 9 September, after which fire destroyed the Greek and Armenian quarters of the city. Facing the Allies at Chanak, Ankara agreed the Armistice of Mudanya, which returned Eastern Thrace to Turkey.

events.name: Battle of Dumlupinar
events.text: The main Greek force was encircled and destroyed on 30 August 1922.

events.name: Great fire of Smyrna
events.text: Fire and killings in September destroyed much of the city, and tens of thousands of Greek and Armenian civilians died or fled.

events.name: Armistice of Mudanya
events.text: The Allies accepted Turkish rule over Eastern Thrace and Constantinople.

steps.label: Nov 1922 to Oct 1923
steps.title: Lausanne and the Republic
steps.text: The Ankara assembly abolished the Ottoman sultanate in November 1922. At Lausanne Ismet Pasha won recognition of Turkish sovereignty over Anatolia and Eastern Thrace, and Greece and Turkey agreed a compulsory exchange of about 1.6 million people. Allied troops left Constantinople, Turkish troops entered it, and on 29 October 1923 the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed with Kemal as president.

events.name: Treaty of Lausanne
events.text: Signed on 24 July 1923, it replaced Sevres and fixed Turkey's borders.

events.name: Proclamation of the Republic
events.text: The assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey with Ankara as its capital.

name: Chinese Civil War
summary: The Nationalist Kuomintang under Chiang Kai-shek and the Chinese Communist Party fought for control of China in two rounds, from the 1927 split to the Japanese invasion and again from 1946. The Communists survived encirclement through the Long March, grew behind Japanese lines during the war with Japan, and then won in Manchuria and in the great Huaihai campaign. In 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China and the Nationalist government withdrew to Taiwan.

steps.label: Apr 1927 to Dec 1928
steps.title: The split and the end of the Northern Expedition
steps.text: Halfway through the Northern Expedition against the warlords, Chiang Kai-shek turned on his Communist allies and massacred them in Shanghai in April 1927. Communist-led units rose at Nanchang on 1 August, the birth of the Red Army, and survivors under Zhu De joined Mao Zedong in the Jinggang Mountains. Chiang's armies took Beijing in June 1928 and the Manchurian warlord accepted Nationalist rule that December.

moves.label: From the Nanchang Uprising to Jinggangshan

events.name: Shanghai massacre
events.text: Nationalist troops and gangsters killed thousands of Communists and labour activists from 12 April 1927.

events.name: Nanchang Uprising
events.text: Communist-led units seized the city on 1 August before being driven south.

events.name: Nationalists take Beijing
events.text: The capture of Beijing ended the Northern Expedition and nominally reunified China.

steps.label: 1930 to Oct 1935
steps.title: Encirclement and the Long March
steps.text: From the Jiangxi Soviet around Ruijin the Red Army beat four Nationalist encirclement campaigns, but Chiang's fifth, ringing the base with blockhouses, forced it to break out in October 1934. About 86,000 men set out on the Long March, lost heavily crossing the Xiang River, and at Zunyi in January 1935 Mao gained a leading voice. A year later fewer than 10,000 reached northern Shaanxi, which became the new Communist base.

events.name: Battle of the Xiang River
events.text: Crossing under fire, the Red Army lost more than half its strength.

events.name: Zunyi Conference
events.text: Party leaders blamed the defeats on their military advisers and Mao rose to the leadership.

events.name: End of the Long March
events.text: The survivors reached the Shaanxi base in October 1935 after about 9,000 km.

steps.label: Dec 1936 to 1945
steps.title: The Xi'an Incident and the United Front
steps.text: In December 1936 Chiang was detained at Xi'an by his own generals and agreed to stop fighting the Communists and resist Japan together. During the war with Japan the Communist Eighth Route and New Fourth Armies fought a guerrilla war behind Japanese lines and expanded their base areas from Yan'an. The truce was uneasy: in January 1941 Nationalist troops destroyed the New Fourth Army headquarters, and by 1945 the Communists ruled about 90 million people.

moves.label: Eighth Route Army crosses into Shanxi
New Fourth Army in the lower Yangtze

events.name: Xi'an Incident
events.text: Zhang Xueliang held Chiang until he accepted a united front against Japan.

events.name: New Fourth Army Incident
events.text: Nationalist forces ambushed the New Fourth Army headquarters, ending real cooperation.

steps.label: Jun 1946 to Dec 1947
steps.title: War resumes
steps.text: After American mediation failed, Chiang's larger and better armed forces attacked in mid 1946, taking cities across north China and Manchuria and capturing Yan'an in March 1947. The Communists gave up territory to destroy units in the field, annihilating the elite 74th Division at Menglianggu. Lin Biao built up a large army in northern Manchuria, and in August 1947 Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping struck south across the Yellow River to the Dabie Mountains.

moves.label: Northeast army attacks across the Sungari

events.name: Battle of Siping
events.text: Nationalist forces drove the Communists back north of the Sungari in May 1946.

events.name: Fall of Yan'an
events.text: Mao abandoned his capital without a fight and kept moving in northern Shaanxi.

events.name: Battle of Menglianggu
events.text: The Communists destroyed the Nationalists' elite 74th Division in Shandong.

steps.label: Sep 1948 to Jan 1949
steps.title: Liaoshen, Huaihai and Pingjin
steps.text: In three great campaigns the Communists destroyed the best Nationalist armies. Lin Biao took Jinzhou and Shenyang and cleared Manchuria, then swept south to take Tianjin and receive the surrender of Beiping. Between November and January, Su Yu, Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping encircled about half a million Nationalist troops around Xuzhou in the Huaihai campaign and captured their commander Du Yuming.

moves.label: East China Field Army on Xuzhou

events.name: Liaoshen campaign
events.text: The fall of Jinzhou trapped the Nationalist armies in Manchuria, which lost about 470,000 men.

events.name: Huaihai campaign
events.text: The decisive battle of the war opened the road to the Yangtze and Nanjing.

events.name: Surrender of Beiping
events.text: General Fu Zuoyi handed over the old capital intact in January 1949.

steps.label: Apr to Dec 1949
steps.title: The Yangtze crossing and the People's Republic
steps.text: On 21 April 1949 Communist armies crossed the Yangtze on a broad front and took Nanjing, Shanghai and Wuhan within weeks. Lin Biao drove south to Guangzhou while Liu and Deng took Chongqing and Chengdu in the southwest. Mao proclaimed the People's Republic of China in Beijing on 1 October, an assault on Kinmen failed in late October, and in December Chiang's government withdrew to Taiwan.

moves.label: Third Field Army crosses the Yangtze
Second Field Army to the southwest

events.name: Crossing of the Yangtze
events.text: Nanjing, the Nationalist capital, fell on 23 April 1949.

events.name: Proclamation of the People's Republic
events.text: Mao declared the founding of the PRC from Tiananmen on 1 October 1949.

events.name: Battle of Guningtou
events.text: The failed landing on Kinmen ended Communist hopes of a quick invasion of Taiwan.

name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
summary: Fascist Italy invaded Ethiopia, one of Africa's last independent states, from its colonies of Eritrea and Somaliland to build an empire and avenge the defeat at Adwa in 1896. Italian armies with aircraft, artillery and poison gas defeated Emperor Haile Selassie's forces in a series of battles in the north and took Addis Ababa in May 1936. The League of Nations' weak sanctions failed to stop the war, a blow to collective security on the road to World War II.

steps.label: Oct to Dec 1935
steps.title: Invasion
steps.text: On 3 October 1935, without a declaration of war, De Bono's army crossed the Mareb from Eritrea and took Adwa, Aksum and Mek'ele, while Graziani advanced into the Ogaden from Italian Somaliland. The League of Nations condemned Italy and imposed sanctions that excluded oil. In December Ras Imru's Christmas Offensive drove the Italians back at the Dembeguina Pass.

events.name: Capture of Adwa
events.text: Italy took the town where it had been defeated in 1896.

events.name: League of Nations sanctions
events.text: The League named Italy the aggressor but its sanctions left out oil.

events.name: Battle of Dembeguina Pass
events.text: Ras Imru's forces overran an Italian column in the Christmas Offensive.

steps.label: Jan to Mar 1936
steps.title: Badoglio's battles in the north
steps.text: Badoglio replaced De Bono and used massed artillery, aircraft and mustard gas, banned by the Geneva Protocol, against Ethiopian armies and civilians. He destroyed Ras Mulugeta's army at Amba Aradam, then those of Ras Kassa and Ras Seyoum in the Tembien and Ras Imru's at Shire. On 31 March Haile Selassie's own counterattack failed at Maychew, while in the south Graziani defeated Ras Desta and took Neghelli.

events.name: Battle of Amba Aradam
events.text: Ras Mulugeta's army was broken by artillery, bombing and gas in February.

events.name: Battle of Shire
events.text: Ras Imru's army was driven back across the Takazze.

events.name: Battle of Maychew
events.text: The emperor's last major army was defeated on 31 March 1936.

steps.label: Apr to May 1936
steps.title: The fall of Addis Ababa
steps.text: Badoglio's motorised columns drove south through Dessie to Addis Ababa, which they entered on 5 May 1936 as Graziani took Harar. Haile Selassie left by rail for Djibouti and exile, and in June he appealed to the League of Nations in Geneva. Mussolini proclaimed an Italian empire, but resistance fighters kept up a guerrilla war until British and Ethiopian forces freed the country in 1941.

events.name: Fall of Addis Ababa
events.text: Italian troops entered the capital on 5 May 1936.

events.name: Haile Selassie addresses the League
events.text: The emperor warned the League in June 1936 that collective security was at stake.

name: Spanish Civil War
summary: A military coup against Spain's Popular Front government in July 1936 split the country between the Republic and the Nationalist rebels led by Francisco Franco. Germany and Italy sent aircraft and troops to the Nationalists, while the Soviet Union and the International Brigades aided the Republic. The Nationalists conquered Spain region by region and won in April 1939, beginning Franco's dictatorship; about 500,000 people died, many in executions behind both lines.

steps.label: Jul to Nov 1936
steps.title: The coup and the march on Madrid
steps.text: The rising of 17 and 18 July 1936 took Spanish Morocco, Seville and the conservative north and west, but failed in Madrid, Barcelona and most of the east. German and Italian aircraft ferried Franco's Army of Africa across the Strait, and Yague's columns drove north, took Badajoz with mass executions, relieved the Alcazar of Toledo and reached Madrid in November. Miaja's defenders, militias and the first International Brigades held the capital.

moves.label: Army of Africa from Morocco to Madrid
Army of the North toward Madrid

events.name: Battle of Badajoz
events.text: The town fell on 14 August and many hundreds of prisoners and civilians were shot.

events.name: Siege of the Alcazar
events.text: Franco diverted his army to relieve the besieged fortress in Toledo on 27 September.

events.name: Battle of Madrid
events.text: The Republic held the capital, and the war became a long one.

steps.label: Feb to Oct 1937
steps.title: Jarama, Guadalajara and the war in the north
steps.text: Nationalist attacks to cut off Madrid failed at the Jarama and, in March, Italian troops were routed at Guadalajara. Franco turned north: German Condor Legion aircraft bombed Guernica on 26 April, Bilbao fell in June, and Santander and Asturias followed by October. Republican offensives at Brunete and Belchite to relieve the north gained little.

events.name: Battle of Guadalajara
events.text: Republican troops routed Mussolini's expeditionary corps in March 1937.

events.name: Bombing of Guernica
events.text: German and Italian aircraft destroyed the Basque town on market day, killing hundreds of people.

events.name: Fall of Bilbao
events.text: The Basque capital fell on 19 June after its defensive ring was broken.

steps.label: Dec 1937 to Nov 1938
steps.title: Teruel, the Aragon offensive and the Ebro
steps.text: The Republic took Teruel in bitter winter fighting, but the Nationalists retook it in February 1938 and swept through Aragon to reach the Mediterranean at Vinaros in April, cutting Republican Spain in two. In July the Republican Army of the Ebro under Modesto crossed the river in a surprise attack. The Battle of the Ebro, the longest of the war, ended in November with the Republic's army spent.

moves.label: Army of the Ebro crosses the river

events.name: Battle of Teruel
events.text: The Nationalists retook the town in February 1938 after the coldest battle of the war.

events.name: Nationalists reach the sea
events.text: The capture of Vinaros on 15 April split the Republic in two.

events.name: Battle of the Ebro
events.text: Four months of attrition destroyed the Republic's last strategic reserve.

steps.label: Dec 1938 to Apr 1939
steps.title: The fall of Catalonia and Madrid
steps.text: The Nationalist offensive in Catalonia took Barcelona on 26 January 1939, and about 450,000 soldiers and civilians fled into France. In Madrid Colonel Casado overthrew Negrin's government in March in the hope of a negotiated peace, but Franco demanded unconditional surrender. Nationalist troops entered Madrid on 28 March, and Franco declared the war over on 1 April 1939.

moves.label: Retreat of the Republican army and refugees

events.name: Fall of Barcelona
events.text: Nationalist troops entered the city on 26 January 1939 almost unopposed.

events.name: Fall of Madrid
events.text: The capital surrendered on 28 March and the war ended four days later.

name: Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: Japan, which already held Manchuria, launched a full-scale invasion of China in 1937, taking the coast, the great cities and the Yangtze valley, and committing mass atrocities at Nanjing. Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists traded space for time from their wartime capital at Chongqing while Communist guerrillas fought behind Japanese lines, and after 1941 the war merged into World War II. China, with about 15 to 20 million dead, outlasted Japan until its surrender in 1945.

steps.label: Jul to Dec 1937
steps.title: From the Marco Polo Bridge to Nanjing
steps.text: A clash at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beiping on 7 July 1937 grew into full war, and Japanese armies took Beiping, Tianjin and the north China railways to Taiyuan. Chiang threw his best divisions into Shanghai, where three months of fighting ended in a Japanese landing behind them in November. Matsui's armies pursued them to Nanjing, which fell on 13 December, followed by weeks of mass killing and rape of prisoners and civilians.

moves.label: North China Area Army down the railways

events.name: Marco Polo Bridge Incident
events.text: A night clash between Chinese and Japanese troops started the full-scale war.

events.name: Battle of Shanghai
events.text: China lost about 250,000 men but showed it would fight.

events.name: Fall of Nanjing and Nanjing Massacre
events.text: Japanese troops killed tens of thousands to over 200,000 prisoners and civilians in the capital.

steps.label: Jan to Oct 1938
steps.title: Taierzhuang, the Yellow River and Wuhan
steps.text: Li Zongren won China's first major victory at Taierzhuang in April 1938, but Japan took Xuzhou in May. To stop the advance on Zhengzhou, Nationalist troops broke the Yellow River dikes in June, flooding vast areas and killing hundreds of thousands of civilians. Hata's armies advanced up the Yangtze and took Wuhan in October while another force landed near Guangzhou, and the government moved to Chongqing.

moves.label: Landing at Bias Bay to Guangzhou

events.name: Battle of Taierzhuang
events.text: Chinese forces encircled and mauled two Japanese divisions in April 1938.

events.name: Yellow River flood
events.text: Breaching the dikes at Huayuankou slowed Japan but killed an estimated 400,000 to 900,000 civilians.

events.name: Battle of Wuhan
events.text: The largest battle of the early war ended with Wuhan's fall on 25 October.

steps.label: 1939 to 1941
steps.title: Stalemate
steps.text: With its armies spread thin, Japan settled into occupation, bombing Chongqing repeatedly and setting up a puppet government at Nanjing. Xue Yue's armies threw back Japanese attacks on Changsha in 1939 and 1941, and in 1940 Peng Dehuai's Communist Eighth Route Army struck the railways of north China in the Hundred Regiments Offensive, provoking brutal Japanese reprisals. When Japan attacked the United States in December 1941, China's war became part of World War II.

events.name: First Battle of Changsha
events.text: The Japanese drive on Changsha was turned back in October 1939.

events.name: Hundred Regiments Offensive
events.text: Communist forces wrecked railways and mines across north China in late 1940.

events.name: Bombing of Chongqing
events.text: Years of Japanese air raids killed thousands but did not break the wartime capital.

steps.label: Apr to Dec 1944
steps.title: Operation Ichi-Go and the Burma Road
steps.text: Japan's largest offensive of the war, Ichi-Go, overran Henan, took Changsha and, after a 47-day siege, Hengyang, then Guilin and Liuzhou, opening a land corridor to Indochina and seizing American air bases. The Nationalist armies suffered huge losses. In the southwest, Chinese troops trained in India under Stilwell took Myitkyina and Wei Lihuang's Yunnan armies crossed the Salween to reopen the land route to China.

events.name: Defence of Hengyang
events.text: The city held for 47 days before falling in August 1944.

events.name: Battle of Guilin-Liuzhou
events.text: Japan took both cities and their air bases in November.

events.name: Siege of Myitkyina
events.text: Chinese and American troops took the key north Burma town in August 1944.

steps.label: Apr to Sep 1945
steps.title: Japan's surrender
steps.text: Chinese armies won a clear victory in western Hunan in spring 1945 and began retaking ground in the south. On 9 August, three days after the bombing of Hiroshima, Soviet armies invaded Manchuria and overran the Kwantung Army. Japan surrendered on 15 August, its forces in China formally surrendered at Nanjing on 9 September, and Taiwan was handed to China in October.

fronts.label: Manchukuo border at the Soviet attack

events.name: Battle of West Hunan
events.text: Chinese forces stopped the last Japanese offensive aimed at the Zhijiang air base.

events.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria
events.text: Over a million Soviet troops destroyed the Kwantung Army in under two weeks.

events.name: Japanese surrender at Nanjing
events.text: General Okamura surrendered over a million Japanese troops in China on 9 September.

name: World War II
summary: The Allies, led by Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States and China, fought the Axis powers of Germany, Italy and Japan after German and Japanese wars of conquest in Europe and Asia. After early Axis victories the tide turned in 1942 and 1943 at Midway, Stalingrad and El Alamein; Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan in September after the atomic bombings and Soviet entry into the war. The deadliest conflict in history, with 70 to 85 million dead including about six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust, it left the United States and the Soviet Union as rival superpowers.

steps.label: Sep 1939 to Mar 1940
steps.title: Invasion of Poland
steps.text: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declared war two days later. German army groups under Bock and Rundstedt converged on Warsaw, and under the Nazi-Soviet Pact the Red Army invaded from the east on 17 September; Poland was partitioned within weeks. In the west the armies faced each other along the Maginot and Siegfried lines in the quiet months of the Phoney War.

moves.label: Army Group North from Pomerania and East Prussia

events.name: Battle of the Bzura
events.text: The largest battle of the campaign ended with the encirclement of two Polish armies.

events.name: Siege of Warsaw
events.text: Warsaw surrendered on 28 September after heavy bombing and shelling.

steps.label: Apr to Jun 1940
steps.title: Blitzkrieg in the west
steps.text: After seizing Denmark and Norway in April, Germany attacked the Netherlands, Belgium and France on 10 May 1940. Guderian's panzers broke through the Ardennes at Sedan and raced to the Channel, trapping the Allied armies in the north, most of whose British troops escaped from Dunkirk. Italy entered the war on 10 June, Paris fell on 14 June, and France signed an armistice that left the north and west under German occupation.

moves.label: Army Group B into the Low Countries
Panzers through the Ardennes to the Channel
British Expeditionary Force falls back to Dunkirk

events.name: Battle of Sedan
events.text: German panzers crossed the Meuse on 13 May and broke the French front.

events.name: Dunkirk evacuation
events.text: About 338,000 British and French troops were evacuated to Britain.

events.name: Armistice of Compiegne
events.text: France signed the armistice on 22 June in the railway carriage used in 1918.

steps.label: Jul 1940 to May 1941
steps.title: Britain stands; the desert and the Balkans
steps.text: The RAF defeated the Luftwaffe's bid for air control over Britain, ending invasion plans, though the Blitz on British cities went on into 1941. In North Africa O'Connor's small British force routed the Italians, then Rommel's Afrika Korps drove the British back to Egypt and besieged Tobruk, while British and Commonwealth forces freed Ethiopia. In April 1941 Germany overran Yugoslavia and Greece, and in May took Crete from the air.

moves.label: Afrika Korps to the Egyptian border

events.name: Battle of Britain
events.text: RAF Fighter Command beat the Luftwaffe over southern England.

events.name: Battle of Beda Fomm
events.text: British forces cut off and destroyed the retreating Italian Tenth Army.

events.name: Battle of Crete
events.text: German paratroopers took the island at such cost that Hitler ended large airborne drops.

steps.label: Jun to Dec 1941
steps.title: Operation Barbarossa
steps.text: On 22 June 1941 Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union with over three million men, encircling whole Soviet armies, besieging Leningrad and taking Kiev. Behind the front, German killing squads began shooting Jews en masse, the start of the Holocaust's systematic phase. The offensive stalled in the autumn mud, and in December Zhukov's counteroffensive threw the Germans back from Moscow.

moves.label: Army Group South to Kiev and Rostov

events.name: Battle of Kiev
events.text: The Germans encircled the city's defenders and took over 600,000 prisoners.

events.name: Babi Yar massacre
events.text: German units shot about 33,000 Jews from Kiev in two days in September 1941.

events.name: Battle of Moscow
events.text: The Red Army halted the drive on Moscow and threw it back in winter.

steps.label: Dec 1941 to Jun 1942
steps.title: Pearl Harbor to Midway
steps.text: On 7 December 1941 Nagumo's carriers struck the US fleet at Pearl Harbor, and the United States entered the war. In six months Japan took Hong Kong, Malaya, Singapore, the Philippines, the Dutch East Indies and Burma. The advance was checked at the Coral Sea in May, and at Midway in June American carriers sank four Japanese carriers, ending Japan's naval superiority.

events.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.text: Japanese aircraft sank or damaged eight battleships and killed about 2,400 Americans.

events.name: Fall of Singapore
events.text: About 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops surrendered on 15 February 1942.

events.name: Battle of Midway
events.text: American carrier aircraft sank four Japanese carriers in a single day.

steps.label: Jun 1942 to Feb 1943
steps.title: Stalingrad and El Alamein
steps.text: Germany's summer offensive drove toward the Caucasus oil fields and the Volga, where Paulus's Sixth Army fought for Stalingrad street by street until a Soviet pincer encircled it in November; it surrendered on 2 February 1943. In Egypt Montgomery's Eighth Army broke Rommel's line at El Alamein, and Eisenhower's Anglo-American landings in Morocco and Algeria trapped the Axis in Tunisia. In the Pacific the Americans won the long struggle for Guadalcanal, while in occupied Europe the Nazi death camps were murdering Jews deported from across the continent.

moves.label: Army Group A into the Caucasus
Eighth Army from El Alamein to Tunisia
Operation Torch and the drive on Tunis

events.name: Battle of Stalingrad
events.text: About 90,000 survivors of the Sixth Army surrendered on 2 February 1943.

events.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
events.text: Montgomery's victory ended the Axis threat to Egypt and Suez.

events.name: Guadalcanal campaign
events.text: Six months of land, sea and air battles ended with Japan's withdrawal in February 1943.

steps.label: Jul 1943 to May 1944
steps.title: Kursk, Italy and island hopping
steps.text: Germany's last great offensive in the east failed at Kursk in July 1943, and the Red Army advanced to the Dnieper, retook Kiev and lifted the siege of Leningrad. After the Axis surrender in Tunisia, the Allies invaded Sicily and then Italy, which changed sides in September, but German troops held the Gustav Line at Cassino for months. In the Pacific Nimitz's forces took Tarawa and the Marshall Islands while MacArthur advanced along New Guinea.

fronts.label: Allied line in the Pacific, early 1944

moves.label: Advance to the Dnieper and Kiev

events.name: Battle of Kursk
events.text: The largest tank battle in history ended Germany's ability to attack in the east.

events.name: Invasion of Sicily
events.text: The Allied landings of 10 July led to Mussolini's fall two weeks later.

events.name: Battle of Tarawa
events.text: US Marines took the fortified atoll in three days of costly fighting.

steps.label: Jun to Dec 1944
steps.title: D-Day, Bagration and Leyte
steps.text: On 6 June 1944 Eisenhower's Allied armies landed in Normandy, broke out in August and liberated Paris and Brussels. On 22 June the Soviet Operation Bagration destroyed Germany's Army Group Centre and carried the Red Army to the Vistula, while Romania and Bulgaria changed sides; that summer about 430,000 Hungarian Jews were deported to Auschwitz. In December Hitler's Ardennes counteroffensive was halted, and in the Pacific the Americans took Saipan and won the naval battle of Leyte Gulf.

events.name: D-Day landings
events.text: About 156,000 Allied troops landed in Normandy on 6 June 1944.

events.name: Operation Bagration
events.text: The Soviet offensive destroyed Army Group Centre and freed Belarus.

events.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
events.text: The largest naval battle in history broke the Japanese fleet.

steps.label: Jan to Jun 1945
steps.title: The fall of Germany
steps.text: The Red Army swept from the Vistula to the Oder in January, liberating Auschwitz, while the Western Allies crossed the Rhine in March and raced into Germany, uncovering concentration camps. Soviet armies under Zhukov and Konev stormed Berlin, Hitler killed himself on 30 April, and Germany surrendered unconditionally on 8 May 1945. In the Pacific, US forces took Iwo Jima and Okinawa in some of the war's bloodiest fighting.

moves.label: Across the Rhine to the Elbe

events.name: Liberation of Auschwitz
events.text: Soviet troops freed the largest Nazi death camp, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, had been murdered.

events.name: Battle of Berlin
events.text: The city fell on 2 May, and Germany surrendered six days later.

events.name: Battle of Okinawa
events.text: Over 200,000 soldiers and civilians died before the island fell in June 1945.

steps.label: Aug to Sep 1945
steps.title: Hiroshima and Japan's surrender
steps.text: American B-29s dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, and the Soviet Union declared war and invaded Manchuria and northern Korea. Emperor Hirohito announced Japan's surrender on 15 August. The formal surrender was signed aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on 2 September 1945, ending the war.

fronts.label: Manchukuo border at the Soviet attack, 9 Aug 1945

moves.label: Enola Gay from Tinian to Hiroshima
Allied occupation forces to Tokyo Bay

events.name: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
events.text: The first nuclear weapon used in war killed about 70,000 to 140,000 people by the end of 1945.

events.name: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki
events.text: The second bomb killed about 40,000 to 75,000 people.

events.name: Surrender of Japan
events.text: Japan signed the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri on 2 September 1945.
